page: Amazon Web Services r6in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, the system provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The processor package incorporates 54 MB of Level 3 cache, 1 MB of Level 2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 512 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is provisioned with a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local instance storage is not included, requiring external EBS volumes for persistent block storage.

Benchmark evaluations position the r6in.16xlarge strongly in cryptographic routines, database transactions, and parallel code execution. PassMark testing highlights top-quartile performance in CPU encryption (56,645.26) and database operations (26,410.42), mirrored by strong results in Geekbench Clang compilation (41,690.0) and ray tracing (58,293.0). Memory throughput tests measured 166.24 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 67.38 GB/sec for write blocks, alongside cached read throughput exceeding 3.3 TB/sec. Text generation benchmarks for small and medium-parameter language models also register in the top 25%, while general single-core stress-ng and Geekbench metrics remain in the median range.

With 512 GB of RAM and 100 Gbps networking without bundled local NVMe disks, the resource profile prioritizes in-memory computation and network throughput over local disk I/O. The platform provides strong throughput efficiency for enterprise databases, distributed in-memory caches, big data analytics engines, and memory-bound compilation pipelines relying on decoupled EBS storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and delivers a 100 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. There is no bundled local instance storage, directing all disk I/O through external EBS infrastructure. In benchmark testing, the system demonstrates top-quartile capability in PassMark database operations, cryptographic execution, Clang compilation, and static web serving throughput reaching 46.07 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth registers at 166.24 GB/sec on uncached datasets. The configuration suits high-scale in-memory caching layers, enterprise relational databases, distributed analytics engines, and network-intensive memory-bound workloads.
